calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in 7 of the last 8 quarters (MarketBeat).
downside: CNBC (16 Nov): board not considering Huang's return; outside law firm reviewing his conduct (The Next Web).
Huang resigned on 12 Nov; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and a permanent search is under way (Nvidia 8-K). Shares closed at $166.19 after a $148.80 low (CoinDesk).
WSJ reported on 11 Nov the board is preparing to oust Huang; shares fell about 8% after hours to around $160 (Yahoo Finance, StockTitan).
Three customers are 44% of revenue; purchase commitments up to $279bn; gross margin guided lower; no China data-centre sales assumed (XTB).
The board opened an independent probe on 8 Nov into reports Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence; House chairs want a briefing on 18 Nov (NBC, FourWeekMBA).
Trump said on 9 Nov the FBI is looking into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy, though he said he believes Huang (Al Jazeera).

history_sources.name: Regards of Wall Street NVDA earnings moves

key_metrics.why: Beating its own guide is expected
Historically the main driver of the move

means: Nvidia guided $108bn revenue and a 74% gross margin; the consensus ($108.8bn) is only just above its own guide.
It beat in 7 of the last 8 quarters but the shares fell after 5 of them. What moves it is the outlook for the next quarter, not the beat.
Last quarter it rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts. That is the pattern to look for.
Its results also move your grid ETF and your Vanguard fund, where Nvidia is one of the largest holdings.
past_notes: Q1 FY26: EPS shown as a miss only because of a $4.5bn China export charge; underlying EPS $0.96 beat.
Q2 FY27 (Aug): rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts.

result.headline: Beat on revenue, EPS and guidance, but shares closed 2.9% lower on 18 Nov after a 4.8% after-hours gain
points: Revenue $115.8bn vs ~$109bn expected (+103% a year); adjusted EPS $2.68 vs ~$2.48 (TipRanks).
Next-quarter guide $130bn ±3% vs ~$125bn expected, a quarter with an extra week (Nvidia release, Coinpaper).
Gross margin guided down to 71-72% from 74.9%, and still no China data-centre sales assumed (Nvidia release).
The 4.8% extended-trading gain reversed: shares closed down 2.89% at $150.96, which Yahoo Finance ties to leadership worries after Huang's exit.
For you: strong numbers did not lift the shares this time; sources say the CEO question is what investors are focused on. Nvidia is also VWRP's largest holding.

upside: Last quarter's guide was well above consensus, and the CFO pointed to ~70% growth in FY28 vs ~44% expected (XTB).

key_metrics.why: It has beaten its guide every quarter here
Future contracted revenue: the market's worry
Cuts here would hit the shares

means: Autodesk beat forecasts in all 8 of the last quarters, but the shares rose after only 4.
In its last two reports it beat yet fell about 4% each time, because full-year guidance came in light and future contracted revenue (cRPO) slowed to 12% growth from 18-20%.
So the key numbers are cRPO and the free-cash-flow guide ($2.725-2.750bn for the year), not the EPS beat.
You hold it for a few months, so this report falls inside your holding window.

stories.headline: Nvidia ends its worst week since 2008, down 23%, as the SEC accounting report adds to post-Huang turmoil

impacts.why: Down 23% in the week to $125.53, its worst week since the 2008 financial crisis and about 48% below its October record (source 1).

sources.title: Nvidia suffers worst week since 2008, as SEC probe report fuels post-Huang turmoil
Exclusive: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say

stories.summary: Reuters reported on Friday that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia; the Wall Street Journal had earlier reported an investigation but not its focus. Nvidia closed at $125.53, down 14% on the day and 23% on the week, its seventh weekly fall in a row and nearly 48% below its 6 Oct record. The report notes an SEC investigation does not establish wrongdoing and can close without action; Nvidia did not immediately comment, and CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO after Jensen Huang's 12 Nov departure.

sources.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler, sources say

stories.summary: Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler, which has a market value of about $33.5bn; the talks could still end without a deal. Zscaler rose 17% and CrowdStrike fell 8% in after-hours trading on Friday. Neither company had responded to requests for comment.
